description:
**We offer competitive salary, great benefits, and work that matters to our community.**
  
  
**The Organization:** The Seattle Housing Authority (SHA) is a mission-driven leader in affordable housing, headquartered on Elliott Avenue West with sweeping views of Elliott Bay and the Puget Sound. With additional field offices across Seattle, we’re committed to expanding housing opportunities, strengthening communities, and supporting a workplace where people grow and thrive.

**The position:** We’re looking for a **Senior HR Analyst** to join our Employee Relations & Labor Relations team! This role will primarily lead and conduct employee investigations and play a key part in strengthening workplace relationships across the agency. The Senior HR Analyst supports the design and execution of HR programs and policies under the guidance of the Labor Relations Manager, with responsibilities spanning employee relations, labor relations, and performance management.

We’re seeking someone who is passionate about resolving workplace issues, supporting fair and thorough investigations, and helping supervisors and employees build effective, trust-based working relationships. The Senior HR Analyst advises departments on complex HR matters, develops and delivers training, and coordinates special projects. The role may also serve as acting Labor Relations Manager when needed.

**The Location:** 101 Elliott Ave W, Seattle, WA 98119

**The ideal candidate will have:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration or Behavioral Science
  + Includes one year of supplemental college-level coursework in Human Resources
  + *OR* an additional four years of relevant work experience may substitute for the degree
* Minimum of six years of progressive experience as an HR Analyst or Business Partner.
* Direct experience should include work in:
  + Labor Relations & Negotiation
  + Employee relations and workplace investigations
  + Performance Management best practices and models
  + HR strategy and program development
  + Policy and procedure development
* Working knowledge of these areas is desired:
  + Classification or Compensation Management
  + Benefits and Leave Management
  + Training

**What will you do?**

* Support the development and implementation of HR programs and ensure compliance with laws and policies.
* Support employee relations and investigations and advise departments on complex HR related matters.
* Participate in labor relations activities and contract interpretation.
* Design and deliver HR-related training to staff and management.
* Contribute to policy development, special projects, and internal communications.
* Monitor legal compliance and provide related staff training.
* Maintain detailed records and generate reports on key HR metrics.
* Use HRIS and Microsoft Office tools to manage data and systems.

These duties are a representation of the essential duties and are not all-inclusive of work assignments or activities.

  

**Application Tips:**

* Update the Work Experience and Education sections with your most current information. *Note: SHA does not accept external attachments such as resumes or cover letters.*

* Complete the Agency-Wide questions. Even if you’ve applied to SHA before, please review and update your responses.

* Respond to any Supplemental Questions, if applicable.

**Why Should You Apply?**

* **Our Culture:** SHA offers a supportive, energetic workplace where collaboration and growth thrive. Our talented team has helped make us a nationally recognized leader in affordable housing and community development.
* **Competitive Salary**
* **Comprehensive Benefits**

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* Public Employees’ Retirement System (PERS)
* Generous paid leave and holidays

* **Work-Life Balance**

* Reasonable hours
* Opportunity for part-time remote work (dependent on the position)

* **Professional Development**

* On-the-job training and growth opportunities

-

**Our Commitment to Equity**

SHA values your unique background and perspective - we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every listed qualification. Learn more in our diversity and application equity statement.

  

**Benefits**
  
Seattle Housing Authority (SHA) is pleased to offer an excellent benefits package for Regular and Project full-time and part-time employees scheduled to work at least 80 hours per month. (Temporary and On-Call positions are not eligible for the full benefits package).
  
  
The following is a brief summary of the SHA benefit programs:
  
  
**Eligibility**
  
As a new hire, your coverage begins on the first calendar day of the month if your hired date is on the first of that month. Otherwise, your coverage begins on the first of the following month.
  
  
**Medical**
  
Employees may select from four medical plans – Kaiser Permanente Standard Plan, Kaiser Permanente Deductible Plan, City of Seattle Preventive Plan, and City of Seattle Traditional Plan.
  
  
The monthly cost for each of the plans are as follows:
  
  
Kaiser Permanente Standard Plan is $48.40 with or without children or $99.90 with spouse/domestic partner with or without children
  
  
Kaiser Permanente Deductible Plan is $25.00 with or without children or $56.92 with spouse/domestic partner with or without children
  
  
City of Seattle Preventive Plan is $48.12 with or without children or $98.50 with spouse/domestic partner with or without children
  
  
City of Seattle Traditional Plan is $0 with or without children or $32.34 with spouse/domestic partner with or without children
  
  
**Dental**
  
Employees may select from two dental plans - Delta Dental, an incentive plan, or Dental Health Services, a managed care plan. Our dental plans include coverage for eligible dependents and are paid for by SHA.
  
  
**Vision**
  
SHA offers two vision plans through VSP Vision Care. The Basic plan is fully paid for by SHA. The Vision Buy-Up plan is paid for by the employee. The Buy-Up plan provides more frequent coverage of lenses, frames, and contact lenses and includes coverage of progressive lenses.
  
  
**Long Term Disability Insurance**
  
If you are disabled, the Basic Plan will be combined with other sources of income to pay you up to $400 a month after a 90-day waiting period. Employees may purchase long-term disability coverage that provides up to 60% of gross monthly salary during disability.
  
  
**Group Term Life (GTL) Insurance**
  
You can select from one of two plans - Basic GTL, which is one-and-a-half times your annual earnings or Limited Basic GTL of $50,000.00. SHA will contribute 40% of the cost for the GTL insurance.
  
  
If you have elected Basic GTL, you may purchase supplemental term life insurance for yourself, your spouse/domestic partner, and your dependent children. The maximum amount of supplemental life insurance available is four times your annual income for the employee, 50% of the amount of coverage you elect for the spouse, and $2,000, $5,000 or $10,000 for children.
  
  
**Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) Insurance**
  
SHA offers an employee-paid group AD&D insurance plan. An employee may cover themself or a family member for amounts from $25,000 to $500,000 in $25,000 increments. AD&D insurance pays a death benefit if the insured person dies due to an accident or a percentage of the full insurance amount if the covered person loses a limb.
  
  
**Retirement Plan**
  
Public Employees' Retirement System (PERS) membership is defined by Washington State statutes and is mandatory if you are hired into an eligible position. However, if you are retired from or have been a member of the City of Seattle, Spokane or Tacoma Employee's Retirement System, your PERS enrollment must be verified and approved by the Washington State Department of Retirement System.
  
  
**Flexible Spending Account (FSA)**
  
Employees have the option of making pre-tax contributions to pay for IRS eligible expenses. There are two accounts: a Health Care Flexible Spending Account and a Dependent Care Flexible Spending Account. Employees can sign up for one or both accounts.
  
  
**Leave Benefits**
  
Annual Leave is provided for vacation and personal time off. First year employees earn up to 3.84 hours per bi-weekly pay period (100 hours annually), increasing incrementally due to service years - up to 7.69 per hours per pay period at 25 years of service (200 hours annually). Leave hours for part time staff are pro-rated. There is a 240-hour annual carryover limit for annual leave.
  
  
Sick leave is provided for health care and related appointments. Employees earn 3.69 hours per pay period. Hours for part time staff are pro-rated. There is no maximum or carryover limit for sick leave.
  
  
Seattle Housing Authority has twelve legal, as detailed below.
  
  
New Year's Day

Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Day

Presidents Day

Memorial Day

Juneteenth

Independence Day

Labor Day

Indigenous People's Day

Veterans Day  
  

Thanksgiving Day

The day following Thanksgiving

Christmas Day
  
  
Additionally, up to three personal holidays are granted to regular employees each calendar year. They are available to be scheduled in advance by the employee with supervisor approval.
  
  
Regular administrative non-represented employees hired between January 1 and May 31 are granted three personal holidays. If hired from June 1 until November 10, two personal holidays are granted. If hired beginning November 11 or later, no personal holidays are granted until January 1.
  
  
**Pay for Performance Program & Merit Awards**
  
Regular Administrative non-represented staff are eligible for Merit Pay and Merit Leave awards based on their annual performance evaluation, as well as on the agency's fiscal year performance from January through December of each year. An employee's merit awards are based on the employee's performance rating, the position of the employee's salary within the salary range, and the fiscal performance of the agency. For new and promoted employees, the merit awards will be pro-rated based on length of time in the current position during the calendar year.
  
  
**Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF)**
  
As an SHA employee, you may be eligible for federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness. This federal program was created to assist full-time public service professionals in reducing their federal student loan debt burden.
  
  
**Employee Transportation Program**
  
A fully subsidized commuter ORCA Passport is offered for use on Metro, Community Transit, Pierce Transit, Kitsap Transit, Everett Transit, Sound Transit, Link Light Rail, Sounder Commuter Train routes. It can also be used on the Seattle Center Monorail. ORCA Passport also provides reduced or fully covered fares on most vanpool routes.
  
  
Additionally, an Emergency Ride Home Program, bike racks at various sites, and shower facilities at several offices are also provided, along with discount Zipcar membership (if accepted). Finally, group discount parking is available for registered vanpools in certain areas.
  
  
**Flex-Time**
  
With supervisor approval, work hours may be scheduled around core hours of 8:00 am to 5:00 pm or a compressed 4/10 workweek. This option is not available for every position.
  
  
**Telework**
  
With supervisor approval, employees can perform assigned duties from home at certain times. This option is not available for every position.
  
  
**Employee Assistance Program**
  
Confidential counseling, referral, and information services are available through ComPsych.
  
  
**Washington Deferred Compensation Program**
  
Tax deferred savings plans are available through the Washington State Department of Retirement Systems' Deferred Compensation Program.

title: Director, People Operations / Human Resources (Hybrid)
description:
About the Role
  
  
The Geneva Foundation is seeking an innovative Director of People Operations & Human Resources to help shape how we attract, develop, engage, and retain the people who advance our mission. We are looking for a forward-looking People & Business Partner who understands that people strategy is business strategy. Working closely with the COO and Leadership Team, the Director will translate Geneva's strategic priorities into a scalable workforce strategy, modern people practices, and an employee experience that enables high performance. Geneva operates in the complex environment of federal government contracting, military medicine, research, and nonprofit mission delivery. Our workforce must be prepared to respond to changing customer requirements, program growth, new business opportunities, evolving technology, and a competitive talent market. The successful candidate will think strategically, operate pragmatically, use data to drive decisions, challenge conventional thinking, and get things done.
  
  
This full-time hybrid position offers a flexible schedule of 2 in-office days and 3 remote workdays per week. Candidates must be based near one of our corporate offices in Bethesda, MD; Frederick, MD; Tacoma, WA; or Fayetteville, NC and be able to regularly work on site/in office as required. Preference is given to candidates residing in the DMV region. Background check will be administered.  
  
Salary Range  
  
$135,000 - $155,000. Salaries are determined based on several factors including external market data, internal equity, and the candidate’s related knowledge, skills, and abilities for the position.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business, Organizational Development, or related field
* 8+ years of progressive HR/People Operations experience, including leadership responsibility
* Demonstrated experience serving as a strategic HR partner to senior leadership
* Strong business acumen and the ability to connect workforce decisions to organizational performance, financial sustainability, and growth
* Strong knowledge of talent acquisition, employee relations, performance management, compensation, benefits, organizational development, and employment compliance
* Experience developing workforce strategies and leading organizational change
* Strong analytical, communication, relationship-building, and problem-solving skills
* Ability to manage sensitive information with discretion and exercise sound independent judgment
* Experience overseeing employee benefits and total rewards programs, including vendor management, benefits strategy, cost analysis, compliance, and employee communications
* Experience with Workday
* Experience leveraging technology, automation, or AI to modernize HR processes

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree in HR, Business, Organizational Development, or related field
* SHRM-SCP, SPHR, PHR, or comparable certification
* Experience in federal government contracting, defense, military medicine, healthcare, scientific research, or another highly regulated environment

**Key Responsibilities**

* Serve as a trusted strategic advisor to the COO and Leadership Team on workforce, talent, and organizational matters
* Develop and execute a People strategy aligned with Geneva's strategic plan, growth objectives, financial priorities, and evolving workforce needs
* Partner with Program and Business Development leaders to anticipate workforce requirements associated with new business, contract growth, and organizational expansion
* Lead talent acquisition, workforce planning, retention, succession planning, leadership development, and employee engagement
* Build proactive talent pipelines and improve the speed, quality, and effectiveness of recruiting
* Strengthen the employee experience from recruitment through career development and retention
* Lead the strategy, administration, and continuous improvement of Geneva's employee benefits programs, including group health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, retirement plans, wellness programs, and other employee benefits
* Evaluate benefits offerings, costs, utilization, competitiveness, and employee needs; recommend changes that balance employee value, market competitiveness, and organizational affordability
* Manage relationships with benefits brokers, carriers, consultants, and other third-party providers and ensure effective vendor performance and service delivery
* Oversee benefits enrollment, communications, compliance, and employee education to ensure employees understand and effectively utilize available programs
* Lead the evolution of performance management, compensation, benefits, and recognition programs
* Use workforce data and analytics to identify trends, measure organizational health, and support better business decisions.
* Lead organizational effectiveness, change management, and culture initiatives
* Modernize People Operations through technology, automation, and use of AI
* Provide guidance on employee relations, employment practices, policies, and compliance, partnering with legal counsel when appropriate
* Ensure People Operations practices comply with applicable federal, state, and local requirements and the unique needs of a federal government contractor
* Lead, develop, and mentor the People Operations team while establishing clear service expectations and performance measures.
* Partner across Finance, Programs, IT, Business Development, Corporate Strategy, and other functions to ensure people strategies support enterprise priorities

**The Leader We're Looking For**

* Strategic but execution-oriented. Can translate strategy into action and measurable results
* A business partner. Understands the connection between people, performance, financial sustainability, and organizational growth
* Forward-looking. Anticipates workforce challenges and opportunities before they become business issues
* Data-driven. Uses meaningful workforce data to inform decisions and measure impact
* A trusted advisor. Comfortable advising, influencing, and respectfully challenging senior leaders
* Innovative. Looks for smarter, simpler, and more effective ways to work
* People-centered. Builds trust, accountability, engagement, and a strong employee experience
* Change-oriented. Can lead people and organizations through growth, transformation, and evolving priorities
* Mission-driven. Understands the importance of Geneva's mission and the people who make it possible

**Why Geneva?**

The Geneva Foundation is a mission-driven nonprofit supporting military medicine, research, and innovation. Our people are at the center of that mission. This is an opportunity to join the Leadership Team and help shape how Geneva attracts, develops, engages, and retains the talent needed for its next stage of growth. If you're ready to help build a modern People function and want your work to have a direct impact on both an organization and its mission, we want to hear from you.

title: Human Resources Manager
description:
***Arboreal Management*** is an affordable housing owner, developer, and property manager across Washington and Oregon. We manage roughly 8,500 units with about 220 employees, and we are growing fast. Alongside our property operations, we build Maynard, our own AI platform for accounting and operations. Our mission is to deliver quality housing people can afford — run by a team that is well supported and well led.

***About the Role***
--------------------

**The Human Resources Manager** leads Arboreal Management's human resources function, providing both strategic direction and hands-on support across a workforce of approximately 220 in Seattle, Portland, Tacoma, and the Philippines, comprising both employees and independent contractors. Arboreal Management is a mission-driven housing firm managing approximately 8,500 units across company-owned properties and third-party management contracts. This role owns the full scope of HR operations — recruiting, onboarding, payroll, performance management, compensation and benefits, employee relations, compliance, training and development, and HR analytics — and is responsible for building a well-run, compliant, and scalable HR function that keeps pace with the company's growth. The position supervises the Recruiter and the Payroll Administrator and is accountable for the results of both functions. The Human Resources Manager partners closely with leadership and managers across the organization, using data and HR best practices to inform decisions while remaining willing to execute hands-on HR work day to day.

***Duties & Responsibilities***
-------------------------------

***Team Leadership and Functional Oversight***

* Supervise the Recruiter and the Payroll Administrator, carrying out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policy and applicable law — including interviewing, hiring, and training; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining; and addressing complaints and resolving problems

* Hold accountability for recruiting outcomes, including time-to-fill, pipeline health for high-volume frontline roles, source effectiveness, offer-acceptance rates, and candidate experience

* Hold accountability for payroll outcomes, including accuracy, on-time processing of each cycle, and timely resolution of pay discrepancies

* Establish and maintain standards, service levels, and documented procedures for the recruiting and payroll functions

* Review and approve work carrying elevated risk or cost, including offers outside approved ranges and off-cycle or retroactive pay adjustments

* Build depth and cross-coverage within the team so that recruiting and payroll continue uninterrupted during absences

***Recruiting and Onboarding***

* Develop and implement effective recruiting strategies to attract top talent, and oversee the full recruitment cycle from job posting through offer negotiation

* Direct recruiting priorities across corporate and site-level roles, including the high-volume frontline hiring that drives most of the company's headcount growth

* Advise hiring managers on interview quality, selection criteria, and internal candidates, and maintain consistency in offers and compensation across roles

* Create and oversee a comprehensive onboarding program so that new hires are set up for success from day one, and personally facilitate new-hire orientation

* Confirm the intended worker classification for each opening before an offer or engagement letter is issued, and administer the corresponding onboarding paperwork

* Oversee the handoff from accepted offer through first day across the recruiting, payroll, and HR functions

***Employee Relations***

* Serve as the first point of contact for staff across corporate, site, and Philippines-based teams on questions, concerns, and workplace conflicts

* Address employee concerns and conflicts promptly to promote a positive work environment

* Conduct workplace investigations, including intake, witness interviews, contemporaneous documentation, findings, and recommended action

* Coach managers through difficult conversations, performance documentation, performance improvement plans, accommodations, and terminations

* Mediate conflicts between individuals and between teams, and address issues before they escalate

* Identify patterns across complaints, exits, and site-level issues, and escalate systemic problems with recommended remedies

* Maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive personnel information with discretion

***Performance, Training, and Development***

* Develop and implement performance evaluation systems, and administer the review cycle end to end including calibration, scheduling, completion tracking, and follow-up

* Conduct regular performance reviews and coach managers on employee development

* Identify training needs and develop or source programs that enhance skills and support career growth

* Deliver manager training, including guidance on documentation, difficult conversations, and directing staff appropriately

* Support career-path and internal advancement conversations, particularly for site-based staff moving into management

***Compensation, Benefits, and Payroll***

* Oversee compensation and benefits programs, ensuring they remain competitive and aligned with company values

* Administer benefits enrollment, qualifying-event changes, terminations, and annual open enrollment

* Manage leave, accommodations, paid time off, and Washington L&I claims from first notice through return to work

* Oversee payroll processing to ensure accuracy and timeliness, reviewing each cycle before release and resolving exceptions with the Payroll Administrator

* Develop and administer recognition programs, and ensure site-level contributions are visible to company leadership

* Lead company-wide communications and connective events across a geographically distributed workforce, including coordination across time zones with the Philippines-based team

***Compliance, Policy, and Safety***

* Ensure compliance with all relevant employment laws and regulations across the company's Washington and Oregon operations, monitor changes in employment law, and update company policies accordingly

* Ensure hiring and pay practices meet applicable requirements, including pay-transparency and pay-equity obligations

* Maintain personnel files, employment eligibility records, and contractor agreements and tax forms to audit standard

* Maintain required workplace postings, regulatory filings, and assigned compliance training, and support audits and agency inquiries

***HR Analytics and Reporting***

* Collect and analyze HR data to provide insight on workforce trends and inform strategic decision-making

* Track and report retention and turnover by role, location, and manager, and bring the underlying drivers forward with recommended action

* Report human resources, hiring, and payroll results to the Chief Financial Officer on a regular cadence

* Maintain the HRIS as the system of record for workforce data, organizational structure, and documentation

***General***

* Adhere to all company policies and procedures

* Perform other duties as required

***What You Bring***
--------------------

* 7+ years of progressive HR experience with real depth in employee relations.
* Direct experience conducting workplace investigations and documenting them defensibly.
* A track record of coaching managers — not just advising them, but changing how they handle their people.
* Experience running engagement, retention, or culture programs and measuring whether they worked.
* Working knowledge of federal and multi-state employment law, including Washington and Oregon.
* Experience with benefits administration, leave management, and an HRIS.
* Sound judgment and real discretion — you will hold things people tell no one else.
* The credibility to be trusted by a maintenance tech and by the executive team in the same week.
* Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, or SPHR.

***Nice to Have***
------------------

* Experience in property management, affordable housing, hospitality, healthcare, retail, or another distributed, multi-site workforce.
* Experience supporting an offshore or international team.
* Experience with Rippling, or similar HRIS.

***How We Work***
-----------------

These are the values we hire and operate against:

* Inclusion and diversity — we hire inclusively and expect people to be treated fairly.

* Data-based decision making — bring numbers, not impressions.
* Questioning conventional wisdom — look for a better way rather than defending the current one.

***Location and Schedule***
---------------------------

This role is based in Seattle, working from our Eastlake office roughly 2–3 days per week with flexibility to work remotely otherwise. Expect regular travel to properties across Washington and Oregon — being visible to site teams is part of the job — and some coordination with our Philippines-based team outside standard Pacific hours.

***Compensation and Benefits***

$95,000 – $110,000 per year, depending on experience, plus an annual bonus.

title: Recruiter and HR Assistant
description:
***Making People the Center of Their Healthcare Journey.***

At Journey Nursing Services, we believe healthcare is about people first. Our mission is to provide exceptional, person-centered care through a holistic approach that supports not only our clients, but their families, caregivers, and the entire healthcare team.

As a Nurse-Owned, Veteran-Owned, and Women-Owned organization, we are committed to raising the standard of community-based healthcare while investing in the professional growth of our employees.

Our ability to provide exceptional care starts with building an exceptional team. We are seeking an energetic, organized, and people-focused Recruiter and HR Assistant to help us attract, hire, and onboard compassionate caregivers, nurses, and healthcare professionals as Journey Nursing Services continues to grow.

The Recruiter and HR Assistant plays a key role in supporting the continued growth of Journey Nursing Services by developing strong candidate pipelines, coordinating the hiring process, and helping new employees successfully transition into the organization.

This position combines recruiting, candidate engagement, onboarding, orientation support, workforce development, and operational collaboration.

You will work closely with the People Operations Manager, clinical leadership, Scheduling, and other departments to ensure recruiting efforts align with current staffing needs and future growth.

**Journey Nursing Services also supports ongoing professional development through:**

* Home Care Aide (HCA) Courses
* CPR/BLS Courses
* Nurse Delegation Certification
* Continuing Education (CEUs)
* Leadership Development
* Healthcare Workforce Development Opportunities

  

**Compensation & Benefits:**

* Competitive hourly pay
* Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance
* Paid Time Off (PTO)
* Washington Paid Sick Leave
* 401(k) Retirement Plan
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Paid orientation and training
* Continuing Education Opportunities
* CPR/BLS renewal assistance
* Leadership and Professional Development Opportunities

  

**Position Overview:**

As a Recruiter and HR Assistant you will support full-cycle recruitment for caregivers, nurses, and assist with other healthcare and administrative positions across Journey Nursing Services.

You will be responsible for developing candidate pipelines, posting and managing employment advertisements, sourcing and screening applicants, coordinating interviews, communicating with candidates, and helping guide new employees through the onboarding process.

This is a **full-time position based on a 40-hour work week and is primarily office-based**. The regular schedule is generally Monday through Friday during business hours, with flexibility based on hiring events, orientation schedules, recruiting needs, and agency operational priorities.

**Essential Responsibilities:**

Recruitment & Candidate Sourcing

* Support full-cycle recruitment for caregiving, nursing, clinical, and administrative positions.
* Partner with hiring managers and operational leaders to understand current and anticipated staffing needs.
* Create, update, and manage job advertisements across recruiting platforms.
* Source qualified candidates through job boards, community partnerships, schools, workforce programs, hiring events and other recruiting channels.
* Screen applicants and conduct initial candidate interviews.
* Coordinate interviews with hiring managers and clinical leadership.
* Maintain timely, professional communication with candidates throughout the hiring process.
* Build and maintain candidate pipelines for hard-to-fill and high-growth positions.
* Help identify recruiting needs before staffing shortages become critical.

Hiring & Onboarding Support

* Maintain awareness of candidates throughout the hiring and onboarding process.
* Coordinate pre-employment requirements.
* Initiate background checks and credential verification.
* Assist with employment documentation and HRIS onboarding.
* Track completion of required onboarding paperwork.
* Help ensure employees meet applicable hiring and credential requirements before being scheduled.
* Collaborate with the People Operations Manager regarding healthcare hiring compliance.
* Support a positive and organized candidate-to-employee transition.

New Employee Orientation

* Assist with coordinating and facilitating new employee orientation.
* Help introduce employees to Journey Nursing Services' culture, expectations, systems, and resources.
* Assist with caregiver skills review and orientation activities when appropriately trained.
* Coordinate with clinical staff for required competency validation and client-specific training.
* Support new employees during their initial transition into the organization.

Journey University & Training Compliance

* Help ensure newly hired employees complete required onboarding education.
* Monitor completion of assigned orientation and training requirements.
* Assist with Journey University administrative and compliance activities.
* Coordinate with educators and clinical leadership when training requirements are incomplete.
* Support continuing education and workforce development initiatives.

Workforce & Operational Support

* Collaborate with Scheduling and Clinical Operations to understand current staffing priorities.
* Participate in workforce planning and recruiting strategy development.
* Assist with recruitment metrics, hiring reports, and process improvement initiatives.
* Support career fairs, hiring events, school partnerships, and community outreach.
* Assist with employee retention and workforce development projects.
* Participate in organizational growth initiatives and special projects as assigned.

Backup Caregiver & Training Support

When appropriately certified, trained, and competent:

* Assist with caregiver orientation and skills training.
* Maintain or obtain CNA/HCA credentials when required for assigned responsibilities.
* Provide occasional backup caregiving support when operationally necessary.
* Reinforce Journey Nursing Services' standards for compassionate, safe, and professional client care.

  

**Qualifications:**

Required

* Associate degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
* Minimum one year of recruiting, Human Resources, healthcare, customer service, or related experience.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
* Excellent organization, follow-through, and attention to detail.
* Comfortable communicating frequently by telephone, email, and in person.
* Ability to manage multiple candidates and priorities simultaneously.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Outlook, and general computer applications.
* Ability to learn EHR, HRIS, applicant tracking, healthcare, and workforce management systems.
* Reliable transportation.

Preferred

* Bachelor's degree.
* Healthcare recruiting experience.
* Previous professional caregiving experience.
* Home Care, Home Health, Hospice, or Private Duty Nursing experience.
* Current or previous CNA or HCA certification.
* Experience with EHR and HRIS platforms.
* Experience conducting employee orientation or training.
* CPR/BLS certification.
* Nurse Delegation certification.

  

**Professional Expectations:**

The Recruiter is expected to:

* Represent Journey Nursing Services professionally throughout the candidate experience.
* Communicate consistently and respectfully with applicants, employees, and hiring managers.
* Protect confidential employee and applicant information.
* Maintain accurate and timely recruiting and onboarding records.
* Demonstrate initiative, accountability, organization, and follow-through.
* Remain flexible as hiring priorities and operational needs change.
* Promote Journey Nursing Services' culture, mission, and employment opportunities accurately and positively.
* Foster a welcoming, respectful, and inclusive candidate experience.

  

Why You'll Love Working Here!

  

Recruiting at Journey Nursing Services is more than filling open positions. You'll help build the workforce that allows clients to remain safely in their homes and communities.

You'll work directly with leaders across the organization, help create career opportunities for caregivers and nurses, improve the new employee experience, and play an important role in Journey Nursing Services' continued growth.

If you're energized by **people, recruiting, healthcare, problem-solving, and building strong teams**, we'd love to meet you.

Join Journey Nursing Services and help build the team that makes people the center of their healthcare journey.

**Apply today—we look forward to meeting you!**

title: HR Payroll Specialist
description:

**Location:** South King County, Washington  
**Schedule:** Full-time, Monday–Friday, onsite  
**Compensation:** Approximately $26–$35/hour, depending on experience

Opportunity Overview

A growing, multi-state organization is seeking an experienced **Payroll Accountant / Payroll & HR Specialist** to join a small, collaborative HR function and take significant ownership of payroll operations.

This is a payroll-first position supporting approximately **500 employees across 15 states**. Roughly 75% of the role centers on payroll, reporting, reconciliation, benefits deductions and related compliance, with the remaining responsibilities providing exposure to onboarding, benefits administration and general HR operations.

The opportunity is particularly well suited for someone who enjoys the technical side of payroll but wants broader exposure and greater ownership than they may receive in a large, highly siloed organization.

What Makes the Opportunity Different

* Significant ownership of a complex multi-state payroll
* Approximately 500 employees across 15 states
* Direct partnership with HR leadership
* Exposure to multiple compensation structures
* Opportunity to work across payroll, benefits and HR operations
* Growing, acquisition-oriented organization
* Collaborative environment with visibility across functions
* Opportunity to develop broader HR expertise without leaving payroll behind
* Established payroll/HRIS technology environment
* Small-team setting where individual contributions are highly visible

Responsibilities

* Process and support biweekly full-cycle payroll for a multi-state employee population
* Manage payroll for hourly, salaried and variable-compensation employees
* Review earnings, deductions, taxes and other payroll calculations for accuracy
* Reconcile payroll records and investigate discrepancies
* Reconcile benefit deductions and vendor billing, including medical, dental, vision, HSA and FSA programs
* Support federal, state and local payroll tax compliance
* Assist with garnishments, levies and child-support orders as applicable
* Partner with Finance/Accounting on payroll reporting and general-ledger alignment
* Support payroll, financial and retirement-plan audits
* Maintain accurate payroll and employee records
* Assist with new-hire processing and onboarding
* Support benefit enrollment and other administrative HR activities
* Maintain appropriate employment documentation
* Produce payroll and HR reports as needed
* Protect confidential employee and compensation information
* Develop into a dependable payroll partner capable of independently owning assigned processes and deadlines

Ideal Candidate Profile

* 2+ years of hands-on payroll experience
* Experience participating directly in full-cycle payroll
* Multi-state payroll experience strongly preferred
* Experience with ADP Workforce Now or another sophisticated payroll/HRIS platform
* Strong Excel skills, including pivot tables and lookup/reconciliation functions
* Demonstrated ability to reconcile payroll and financial data
* Working knowledge of federal, state and local payroll requirements
* Strong attention to detail and deadline management
* Comfortable troubleshooting payroll discrepancies
* Able to handle confidential employee information professionally
* Reliable and comfortable working in an onsite environment
* Collaborative, accountable and willing to take ownership

Preferred Payroll/Business Characteristics

The strongest candidates will bring experience with several of the following:

* Payroll populations of several hundred employees
* Multi-state or distributed workforces
* Hourly and salaried payroll
* Commission or draw-based compensation
* Benefit deduction reconciliation
* Payroll taxes across multiple jurisdictions
* Garnishments, levies and support orders
* Payroll or financial audits
* 401(k) audit support
* Advanced Excel reconciliation
* ADP Workforce Now
* UKG or comparable enterprise payroll platforms

An associate degree in Accounting, Business, Human Resources or a related field is helpful but not the primary selection criterion.

Not a Fit If You

* Have primarily general HR experience with limited hands-on payroll responsibility
* Have only submitted payroll changes without participating in full-cycle processing
* Are uncomfortable working extensively in Excel
* Do not enjoy reconciliation and detailed payroll work
* Require a remote position
* Are unable to maintain a reliable Monday–Friday onsite schedule
* Prefer a highly siloed position with narrowly defined responsibilities
* Are primarily seeking employee-relations or strategic HR responsibilities

Compensation

The anticipated compensation range is approximately **$26–$35 per hour**, depending on payroll experience, technical capabilities, system knowledge and overall qualifications.

The organization also offers a competitive benefits package that may include medical, dental and vision coverage, life insurance, flexible spending options, supplemental insurance, retirement-plan contributions, paid time off, paid holidays and ongoing training opportunities.

**About the Department of Natural Resources** **(DNR).**

**More than Just a Paycheck!**
  
Employee benefits are not just about the kind of services you get, they are also about how much you may have to pay out of pocket. Washington State offers one of the most competitive benefits packages in the nation.
  
  
We understand that your life revolves around more than just your career. Like everyone, your first priority is ensuring that you and your family will maintain health and financial security. That's why choice is a key component of our benefits package. We have a selection of health and retirement plans, paid leave, staff training and other compensation benefits that you can mix and match to meet your current and future needs.
  
  
**Read about our benefits:**
  
*The following information describes typical benefits available for full-time employees who are expected to work more than six months. Actual benefits may vary by appointment type or be prorated for other than full-time work (e.g. part-time); view the job posting for benefits details for job types other than full-time.*
  
  
**Note:** *If the position offers benefits which differ from the following, the job posting should include the specific benefits.*
  
  
**Insurance Benefits**
  
Employees and their families are covered by medical (including vision), dental and basic life insurance. There are multiple medical plans with affordable monthly premiums that offer coverage throughout the state.
  
  
Staff are eligible to enroll each year in a medical flexible spending account which enables them to use tax-deferred dollars toward their health care expenses. Employees are also covered by basic life and long-term disability insurance, with the option to purchase additional coverage amounts.
  
  
To view premium rates, coverage choice in your area and how to enroll, please visit the Public Employees Benefits Board (PEBB) website. The Washington Wellness program from the Health Care Authority works with PEBB to support our workplace wellness programs.
  
  
Dependent care assistance allows the employee to save pre-tax dollars for a child or elder care expenses.
  
  
Other insurance coverage for auto, boat, home, and renter insurance is available through payroll deduction.
  
  
The Washington State Employee Assistance Program promotes the health and well-being of employees.
  
  
**Retirement and Deferred Compensation**
  
State Employees are members of the Washington Public Employees' Retirement System (PERS). New employees have the option of two employer contributed retirement programs. For additional information, check out the Department of Retirement Systems' web site.
  
  
Employees also have the ability to participate in the Deferred Compensation Program (DCP). This is a supplemental retirement savings program (similar to an IRA) that allows you control over the amount of pre-tax salary dollars you defer as well as the flexibility to choose between multiple investment options.
  
  
**Social Security**
  
All state employees are covered by the federal Social Security and Medicare systems. The state and the employee pay an equal amount into the system.
  
  
**Public Service Loan Forgiveness**
  
If you are employed by a government or not-for-profit organization, and meet the qualifying criteria, you may be eligible to receive student loan forgiveness under the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program.
  
  
**Holidays**
  
Full-time and part-time employees are entitled to paid holidays and one paid personal holiday per calendar year.
  
  
**Note:** Employees who are members of certain Unions may be entitled to additional personal leave day(s), please refer to position specific Collective Bargaining Agreements for more information*.*
  
  
Full-time employees who work full monthly schedules qualify for holiday compensation if they are employed before the holiday and are in pay status for at least 80 nonovertime hours during the month of the holiday; or for the entire work shift preceding the holiday.
  
  
Part-time employees who are in pay status during the month of the holiday qualify for the holiday on a pro-rata basis. Compensation for holidays (including personal holiday) will be proportionate to the number of hours in pay status in the month to that required for full-time employment, excluding all holiday hours. Pay status includes hours worked and time on paid leave.
  
  
**Sick Leave**
  
Full-time employees earn eight hours of sick leave per month. Overtime eligible employees who are in pay status for less than 80 hours per month, earn a monthly proportionate to the number of hours in pay status, in the month to that required for full-time employment. Overtime exempt employees who are in pay status for less than 80 hours per month do not earn a monthly accrual of sick leave.
  
  
Sick leave accruals for part-time employees will be proportionate to the number of hours in pay status, in the month to that required for full-time employment. Pay status includes hours worked, time on paid leave and paid holiday.
  
  
**Vacation (Annual Leave)**
  
Full-time employees accrue vacation leave at the rates specified in WAC 357-31-165(1) or the applicable collective bargaining agreement (CBA). Full-time employees who are in pay status for less than 80 nonovertime hours in a month do not earn a monthly accrual of vacation leave.
  
  
Part-time employees accrue vacation leave hours in accordance with WAC 357-31-165(1) or the applicable collective bargaining agreement (CBA) on a pro rata basis. Vacation leave accrual will be proportionate to the number of hours in pay status, in the month to that required for full-time employment.
  
  
Pay status includes hours worked, time on paid leave and paid holiday.
  
  
As provided in WAC 357-58-175, an employer may authorize a lump-sum accrual of vacation leave or accelerate the vacation leave accrual rate to support the recruitment and/or retention of a candidate or employee for a Washington Management Service position. Vacation leave accrual rates may only be accelerated using the rates established WAC 357-31-165.
  
  
**Note:** Most agencies follow the civil service rules covering leave and holidays for **exempt** employees even though there is no requirement for them to do so. However, agencies are required to adhere to the applicable RCWs pertaining holidays and leave.
  
  
**Military Leave**
  
Washington State supports members of the armed forces with 21 days paid military leave per year.
  
  
**Bereavement Leave**
  
Most employees whose family member or household member dies, or for loss of pregnancy, are entitled to five (5) days of paid bereavement leave. In addition, the employer may approve other available leave types for the purpose of bereavement leave.
  
  
**Additional Leave**
  
Leave Sharing
  
Parental Leave
  
Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA)
  
Leave Without Pay
  
  
Please visit the State HR Website for more detailed information regarding benefits.

title: Human Resources Business Partner II

description:
**About Cascade**

Cascade is a nonprofit community health center that has served Lewis County and the surrounding communities for 60 years. With five locations throughout Lewis County, Washington, we provide a wide range of services designed to meet the needs of our clients and community.

**Position Summary**

Our HR team is seeking an organized, collaborative HR Generalist to support employees and leadership through recruitment, onboarding, payroll, benefits, leave administration, and employee relations. Each generalist manages assigned responsibilities while maintaining broad HR knowledge to provide coverage and support the department. The ideal candidate demonstrates sound judgment, confidentiality, attention to detail, and the ability to manage competing priorities with dependable follow-through.

**Location and Schedule**

* **Location:** 2428 W Reynolds Avenue Centralia, WA 98531
* **FTE/Hours:** 1.0FTE (40-hours)
* **Schedule:** Monday - Friday; start and end times may be flexible based on department needs and supervisor approval. HR office hours are currently Monday - Thursday 7am-4pm & Friday 8am-12:00pm.

  

**Pay Range**

$31.26 - $40.02; starting rate depends on experience and education.

**Qualifications**

* At least three years of human resources experience required; experience across multiple HR functions preferred.
* Bachelor’s degree in human resources, Business Management, or related field preferred.
* Payroll processing experience preferred, with the ability to learn and independently perform full-cycle payroll following training.
* Must be able to pass WA State Patrol background check. A national background check may be required if haven’t lived in WA State for the last 3 consecutive years.
* Ability to represent Cascade in a positive and professional manner and demonstrate the competencies listed above.

  

**Competencies:**

* Clear verbal and written communication; ability to explain HR policies and processes respectfully to employees and leadership.
* Strong interpersonal skills, sound judgment, and a professional approach to conflict resolution.
* Ability to work independently, take ownership of assigned work, and collaborate closely with the HR team.
* Ability to manage competing priorities, meet deadlines, and communicate promptly when additional support or direction is needed.
* Accuracy, attention to detail, and dependable follow-through on time-sensitive tasks.
* Ability to recognize complex or sensitive issues and seek appropriate guidance.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to interpret information and review numerical data.
* Working knowledge of federal and Washington employment laws, with the ability to research requirements and seek guidance.
* Ability to act with integrity, professionalism, and confidentiality and respond constructively to feedback.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and the ability to learn HRIS; includes payroll and applicant tracking systems.

  

**What You'll Do**

* Provides timely, respectful service and HR guidance to applicants, employees, and leadership; refers complex or sensitive matters to the Chief People Officer.
* Manages assigned HR functions, participates in cross-training, and provides coverage during staff absences and changes in department workload.
* Coordinates recruiting activities, including job postings, applicant communication, interview scheduling, and hiring support.
* Coordinates background checks and employment eligibility verification; conducts new hire orientation and supports onboarding and employee separations.
* Participates in full-cycle payroll and independently processes payroll on rotation with HR staff, following established procedures and review requirements.
* Administers employee benefits, including health, dental, vision, flexible spending accounts, life and disability insurance, COBRA, 401(k), and wellness programs.
* Administers assigned employee leave processes, including tracking, documentation, employee communication, and coordination of benefits during leave.
* Maintains accurate, confidential personnel records and HRIS data; processes personnel changes and prepares HR reports.
* Reviews and responds to unemployment claims with supporting documentation. Participate in unemployment hearings as assigned.
* Tracks and documents employee training, continuing education, professional licensure, and certification requirements.
* Supports employee relations, performance management, disciplinary meetings, investigations, and terminations under the direction of the Chief People Officer.
* Supports compliance with federal, Washington State, and local employment requirements; identifies concerns and assists with policy and procedure updates.
* Plans and participates in employee recognition programs, HR activities, and events; supports assigned safety and training programs.
* Maintains current HR knowledge and identifies opportunities to improve department processes and service.
* Performs other duties related to supporting the Human Resources Department as assigned.

  

**What You'll Love About Cascade**

* **Meaningful work:** The services we provide make a meaningful difference in the lives of our clients and throughout our community.
* **Time away from work:** Employees earn up to 13 hours of paid time off each month and receive 11 paid holidays plus 16 hours of personal holiday time. Benefits are prorated based on FTE. PTO and personal holiday hours are available after 90 days of employment.
* **Company-paid employee benefits (2026):** Medical, dental, vision, AllyHealth, employee assistance program, life and AD&D insurance, long-term disability, critical illness, hospital indemnity, and accident insurance, subject to applicable plan terms. Medical coverage is available to employees working at least 0.75 FTE (30 hours per week) and is effective the first of the month following the date of hire. Employees working at least 0.5 FTE (20 hours per week) are eligible for all other applicable benefits.
* **Voluntary benefits:** Supplemental term life insurance, legal services, fraud and identity protection, HSA, FSA, dependent care FSA, and pet insurance, subject to applicable plan terms.
* **Retirement benefits:** After six months of employment, Cascade contributes 5% of your gross earnings to a 401(k) each month—no employee contribution or match is required.

  

**How to Apply**

If you’re interested in joining our team, please submit your resume [and cover letter, if applicable]. No phone calls, please.

title: Human Resource Consultant 4 (HRC4) with option for HRC3 In-Training
description:
**Description**
---------------

**GENERAL SERVICE**

**JOB ANNOUNCEMENT**

  

Human Resource Consultant 4 (HRC4) with option for HRC3 In-Training

$76,608-102,996 annually

  
  

**Recruitment closes October 12, 2026**

  
  

The Washington State Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction (OSPI) seeks to fill a Human Resource Consultant 4 position. This full-time permanent position is based in Olympia, Washington. This position may be eligible for partial telework. **The position will be required to be in the office full-time for onboarding (The onboarding timeline will vary based on the selected candidate's existing skills, experience, and learning pace) after which, the position may be eligible to telework up to two days per week (days of the week to be determined with Supervisor approval).** Telework is a combination of in-building and off-site days. We encourage interested candidates to visit the OSPI website to gain insight into our agency.

**This may be filled as an in-training position*****.****This is designated as a 12-24-month training plan. If you complete all elements of the training steps in less time, we may waive the remaining time required.* *Candidates will be considered as a* ***Human Resource Consultant 3 (HRC3 In-Training) or Human Resource Consultant 4 (HRC4),*** *depending on qualifications.*

  

**About OSPI and our initiatives**

OSPI is the primary agency charged with overseeing public K–12 education in Washington state. Working with the state's 295 public school districts and 7 state-tribal education compact schools, OSPI allocates funding and provides tools, resources, and technical assistance so every student in Washington is provided a high-quality public education.

At OSPI, we recognize that our employees are the key to the success of the agency. We are committed to our work but value the balance with our personal lives. We demonstrate our commitment to employees by providing an environment that stimulates professional growth and values them for their expertise. OSPI is a great place to work and has several initiatives to help create a great working environment, including:

  
  

* We support a healthy work/life balance by offering flexible/alternative work schedules and mobile and telework options. (Depending on job duties and work location.)
* We have an Infant at Work Program that is based on long-term values of newborns and infant-parent bonding. Eligible employees who are new parents or legal guardians can bring their infant (six weeks to six months) when returning to work. (Depending on job duties and work location.)
* We value and are actively involved in promoting diversity, equity and inclusion within OSPI by way of cross-divisional, collaborative committee. The focus of the committee includes employee engagement and education; reinforcing OSPI values; and maximizing the value of diversity and identifying strategies for inclusion.

  

**Vision, Mission, and Values**  
Vision: All students prepared for post-secondary pathways, careers, and civic engagement.
  
  
Mission: Transform K-12 education to a system that is centered on closing opportunity gaps and is characterized by high expectations for all students and educators. We achieve this by developing equity-based policies and supports that empower educators, families, and communities.

  
  

Values: Ensuring Equity, Collaboration and Service, Achieving Excellence through Continuous Improvement, Focus on the Whole Child

  

**Equity**

Each student, family, and community possesses strengths and cultural knowledge that benefits their peers, educators, and schools. Ensuring educational equity:

  
  

* Goes beyond equality; it requires education leaders to examine the ways current policies and practices result in disparate outcomes for our students of color, students living in poverty, students receiving special education and English Learner services, students who identify as LGBTQ+, and highly mobile student populations.
* Requires education leaders to develop an understanding of historical contexts; engage students, families, and community representatives as partners in decision-making; and actively dismantle systemic barriers, replacing them with policies and practices that ensure all students have access to the instruction and support they need to succeed in our schools.

  

**Position Overview**  
This position serves under the direction of the Chief Human Resource and Facilities Officer (CHRFO) as a senior professional consultant, handling the organization’s most sensitive, complex, and critical human resource activities. Responsibilities require application of expert knowledge to advise agency leadership. Assignments require forward thinking mindset, proactive intervention and have agency wide and precedent setting impact. This role also provides advice and guidance to employees on HR processes and is mentor/trainer to other HR peers and staff.

  
  

**In addition to providing consultation to assigned OSPI divisions, this position is responsible for providing the HR services described to the following small agencies:**

* Washington Charter School Commission
* Financial Education Public-Private Partnership
* Professional Educator Standards Board
* State Board of Education
  

**Key Responsibilities**

**Consultation and Compliance**

* Provides advice, interpretation, and counsel to clients regarding applicable human resource civil service rules, regulations, policies, and procedures in areas such as classification, compensation, performance management, grievance resolution, reasonable accommodation, organizational development, recruiting, hiring, benefits, protected leave, Labor and Industries claims, and layoffs.
* Ensures compliance with federal and state employment laws, collective bargaining agreement, and agency policies and procedures. Advises management on best practices in HR actions, consulting with the agency CHRO and/or agency’s assigned Labor and Personnel AAG on most complex liability concerns.
* Research and analyze proposed rules, laws and policies to determine agency impacts, participates in planning, creating and implementing new human resource programs, policies and procedures.
* Develops, implements, and oversees HR policies and procedures, strategic plans, reports, forecasts and projections and statement and reports.
* Assist with the formulation, determination, and effectuation of management policies in the agency and effectuation of employee and labor relations, and is responsible for maintaining confidentiality concerning such matters.
* Conduct and assist other HR staff with employment investigations consistent with agency policies, state and federal laws.
* Meet with administrators, supervisors, and employees to assess human resource needs. Plans, develops, and implements strategies to promote effective client relations and to resolve problems.
* Track and analyze personnel issues and needs; devise plan and approach to supporting change to addressing needs.
* Researches and analyzes proposed rules, laws, and program elements to determine impact on unit or organizational operations; participates in planning and implementing new human resources programs, policies, and procedures.
* Partners with agency administrators to recommend and assist with selection, training, direction, and evaluation of staff, establishing and monitoring standards of performance.
* Provide support regarding organizational culture that supports diversity and promotes inclusion.
  

  

**Classification and Compensation**

* Determines appropriate classification of positions. Partners with management in analyzing organizational structure, developing recommendations for staff configurations to enhance effectiveness, assists with drafting position descriptions. Review existing and updated position descriptions for potential changes in classification. Address requests for appeal of job classification allocations, represent OSPI in appeal hearings.
* Serves as OSPI’s Washington Management Service (WMS) Coordinator and liaison with State HR for all agency WMS activities. Leads the WMS Review committee, including scheduling and running meetings, maintaining committee membership, and training committee members. Provide data to agency leadership and State HR on the agency’s WMS program and compliance with state regulations. Participates in the WMS Review Committee as the external HR representative.
* Conduct compensation analysis for salary alignment and equity purposes. Research and propose salary ranges for new roles, recommend salary placement for new hires and internal promotions, analyze how position changes may affect compensation. Perform scheduled and ad hoc research and updates to compensation plan for WMS and Exempt roles in OSPI.
* Manage the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) application of overtime rules across the agency. Notify management and staff of updates and changes to overtime status.
  

  

**Training and Development**

* Participate in the development and delivery of training or other presentations to staff and management on a variety of human resource topics, processes, rules, policies and procedures.
* Conduct orientation program for new supervisors.
* Stay current on emerging HR topics, knowledge and skills.
  

  

**Special Projects**

* Participates and/or coordinates special projects, committees, or task forces.
* Perform clerical support to Chief Human Resource and Facilities Officer and other HR staff. Provide support in NEOGOV and the Learning Center systems.
* Provide reports and prepare data for presentation to administrators, supervisors, and staff.
  

  

**Required Qualifications:**

**Human Resource Consultant 4 level (range 63 $76,608 – 102,996)**

* A Bachelor’s degree with focus on business, human resources, social or organizational behavioral sciences, or related field AND three (3) years of professional human resource experience as defined below.

**OR**

* (in lieu of degree) Five (5) years professional experience in the majority of these areas:
  + Interpretation and/or explanation of civil service rules and human resource related policies.
  + Corrective and disciplinary actions
  + Classification
  + Labor relations
  + Developing or presenting training or orientation in human resource-related topics
  + Employee recruitment and selection
  + Representing the agency in grievances or appeals
  + Workers compensation
  + Consulting and advising management on human resource issues

  

**Human Resource Consultant 3 level (range 59 $69,348 – 93,288)**

* A Bachelor’s degree with focus on business, human resources, social or organizational behavioral sciences, or related field AND two (2) years of professional human resource experience as defined below.

**OR**

* (in lieu of degree) Four (4) years professional experience in half of these areas:
  + Interpretation and/or explanation of civil service rules and human resource related policies.

Employees and their families are covered by medical (including vision), dental and basic life insurance. There are multiple medical plans with affordable monthly premiums that offer coverage throughout the state.

Other insurance coverage for auto, boat, home, and renter insurance is available through payroll deduction.
  
  
The Washington State Employee Assistance Program promotes the health and well-being of employees.
  
  
**Retirement and Deferred Compensation**
  
State Employees are members of the Washington Public Employees' Retirement System (PERS). New employees have the option of two employer contributed retirement programs. For additional information, check out the Department of Retirement Systems' web site.
  
  
Employees also have the ability to participate in the Deferred Compensation Program (DCP). This is a supplemental retirement savings program (similar to an IRA) that allows you control over the amount of pre-tax salary dollars you defer as well as the flexibility to choose between multiple investment options.
  
  
**Social Security**
  
All state employees are covered by the federal Social Security and Medicare systems. The state and the employee pay an equal amount into the system.
  
  
**Public Service Loan Forgiveness**
  
If you are employed by a government or not-for-profit organization, and meet the qualifying criteria, you may be eligible to receive student loan forgiveness under the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program.
  
  
**Holidays**

**Note:** Employees who are members of certain Unions may be entitled to additional personal leave day(s), please refer to position specific Collective Bargaining Agreements for more information*.*
  
  
Full-time employees who work full monthly schedules qualify for holiday compensation if they are employed before the holiday and are in pay status for at least 80 nonovertime hours during the month of the holiday; or for the entire work shift preceding the holiday.
  
  
Part-time employees who are in pay status during the month of the holiday qualify for the holiday on a pro-rata basis. Compensation for holidays (including personal holiday) will be proportionate to the number of hours in pay status in the month to that required for full-time employment, excluding all holiday hours. Pay status includes hours worked and time on paid leave.
  
  
**Sick Leave**
  
Full-time employees earn eight hours of sick leave per month. Overtime eligible employees who are in pay status for less than 80 hours per month, earn a monthly proportionate to the number of hours in pay status, in the month to that required for full-time employment. Overtime exempt employees who are in pay status for less than 80 hours per month do not earn a monthly accrual of sick leave.
  
  
Sick leave accruals for part-time employees will be proportionate to the number of hours in pay status, in the month to that required for full-time employment. Pay status includes hours worked, time on paid leave and paid holiday.
  
  
**Vacation (Annual Leave)**
  
Full-time employees accrue vacation leave at the rates specified in WAC 357-31-165(1) or the applicable collective bargaining agreement (CBA). Full-time employees who are in pay status for less than 80 nonovertime hours in a month do not earn a monthly accrual of vacation leave.
  
  
Part-time employees accrue vacation leave hours in accordance with WAC 357-31-165(1) or the applicable collective bargaining agreement (CBA) on a pro rata basis. Vacation leave accrual will be proportionate to the number of hours in pay status, in the month to that required for full-time employment.
  
  
Pay status includes hours worked, time on paid leave and paid holiday.
  
  
As provided in WAC 357-58-175, an employer may authorize a lump-sum accrual of vacation leave or accelerate the vacation leave accrual rate to support the recruitment and/or retention of a candidate or employee for a Washington Management Service position. Vacation leave accrual rates may only be accelerated using the rates established WAC 357-31-165.
  
  
**Note:** Most agencies follow the civil service rules covering leave and holidays for **exempt** employees even though there is no requirement for them to do so. However, agencies are required to adhere to the applicable RCWs pertaining holidays and leave.
  
  
**Military Leave**
  
Washington State supports members of the armed forces with 21 days paid military leave per year.
  
  
**Bereavement Leave**
  
Most employees whose family member or household member dies, or for loss of pregnancy, are entitled to five (5) days of paid bereavement leave. In addition, the employer may approve other available leave types for the purpose of bereavement leave.

Leave Sharing
  
Parental Leave
  
Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA)
  
Leave Without Pay

* Professional Educator Standards Board

* Oversee and manage reduced responsibility, and roster percentage changes, ensuring compliance with University, School of Medicine, and regulatory policies.

title: Senior Human Resources Manager
description:
***Arboreal***'s mission is to build community, dignity, and opportunity into every home we manage. We are a mission-driven property management company focused on affordable and workforce housing, caring for roughly 8,500 homes across more than 130 properties in Washington and Oregon — and we are growing fast. Our team of about 220 people, a mix of employees and independent contractors in the Pacific Northwest and the Philippines, is what makes that mission real for our residents every day.

Our teams take care of our residents. This role takes care of our teams. As our Senior Human Resources Manager, you'll bring the same care to the people who keep our properties running — our maintenance technicians, leasing associates, property managers, and the teams behind them — so they're hired well, supported well, and given a real chance to grow.

***The Role***
--------------

This is a people leadership role with a seat at the table. You'll be a trusted advisor to our entire executive team on everything people-related: how we organize as we grow, where we need to strengthen leadership, and the people side of our biggest decisions. We promise our people clear roles, regular feedback, and opportunities to level up — and we're looking for someone who can help us keep that promise as we scale.

You'll have a capable team alongside you. Our Recruiter and Payroll Administrator report to you and run the day-to-day of hiring and payroll, so your energy can go toward the bigger picture: shaping the programs and practices that help our people do their best work.

***Where You'll Focus***
------------------------

Finding the right people. Partnering with our Recruiter and hiring managers to get clear on what great looks like in each of our key roles, reach the candidates who fit, and make hiring decisions with confidence. Quality of hire matters more to us than speed alone.

Helping people grow and perform. Creating a performance approach that feels like ongoing, honest conversation rather than an annual form — and pairing it with onboarding, training, and manager development that help people succeed.

Rewarding what matters. Taking a fresh look at our bonus program and incentive structures — from leasing commissions to annual bonuses — so they reward great resident experiences, strong teams, and performance. This includes helping shape a clear, fair approach to compensation and keeping our benefits competitive.

Keeping people connected. Our people work across more than 130 properties and two countries, as employees and as contractors. Listening to what they need, acting on what we hear, and making sure great work at a property is seen by leadership.

Being the trusted resource. When a manager or team member needs HR — a conduct concern, a complaint, an accommodation, a difficult conversation — you're the person they call. That includes leading workplace investigations with fairness and care, and giving managers practical guidance they can use right away.

Keeping our foundation strong. Making sure we stay compliant with federal, Washington, and Oregon employment law and the local rules in cities like Seattle and Tacoma; keeping our policies and handbook current;

partnering with Operations on safety for our site teams; and turning our HR data into insight leadership can act on — with help from AI and our own proprietary platform wherever it saves time.

***About You***
---------------

* You have 7+ years in HR, including at least 3 leading an HR or people function or a significant part of one
* You've built people programs from the ground up — performance management, training, compensation, or talent strategy — and can tell us what changed because of them
* You've advised senior leaders and are comfortable being a thought partner to an executive team
* You understand frontline and multi-site workforces, and you've supported a mix of employees and contractors
* You've led workplace investigations and kept a company compliant across multiple states and cities
* You think in systems but still enjoy rolling up your sleeves
* You can hold your own with executives and still be someone a maintenance tech trusts

Experience in property management, hospitality, healthcare, or retail, a SHRM or HRCI certification, supporting an offshore team, and comfort using AI to reduce manual HR work are all a plus.

***How We Work***
-----------------

We hire and operate against six values: inclusion and diversity, teamwork, data-based decision making, questioning conventional wisdom, respect, and ownership and initiative. In practice that means we bring numbers rather than impressions, look for a better way rather than defending the current one, and treat people with dignity — especially in hard conversations.

***Good to Know***
------------------

This role is based in Seattle, working from our Eastlake office roughly 2–3 days a week with flexibility to work remotely otherwise. It reports to our CFO and works closely with the full executive team. Expect regular time at our properties across Washington and Oregon — being visible to site teams is part of the job — and some coordination with our Philippines-based team outside standard Pacific hours.

***Compensation is $95,000 – $120,000 per year, depending on experience, plus an annual bonus.***

***Equal Opportunity***
-----------------------

We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodation to applicants with disabilities — let us know if you need one during the hiring process.
